title: Update on Discussion with SPH Media Trust on Funding Support Measures to Ensure Sustainability in Competitive Media Industry and Limited Local Market
what_it_is: Update on Discussion with SPH Media Trust on Funding Support Measures to Ensure Sustainability in Competitive Media Industry and Limited Local Market

sections.label: SPH Media Trust funding and independence
sections.summary: Questions ask about updates on Government discussions with SPH Media Trust, funding support level, ensuring funding achieves digital transformation, and upholding editorial independence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) whether there are any updates from the Government’s discussion with SPH Media Trust and on the level of funding support that the Government will provide; and (b) how will the Government ensure that the funding provided will be used to achieve the necessary digital transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information with the commitment of the Government to provide funding support to SPH Media Trust, how will the Ministry ensure that editorial independence continues to be upheld in the newsrooms.

sections.label: SPH Media Trust relevance and vernacular media
sections.summary: Questions ask how SPH Media Trust stays relevant and sustainable, how local journalism quality keeps pace, desired outcomes and tracking, and viability of vernacular news media.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) how will SPH Media Trust remain relevant and sustainable in a highly competitive media industry given digital disruption and declining demand for print news; (b) how can the quality of local journalism keep pace with global standards since audiences can easily access digital versions of international newspapers; and (c) what are the desired outcomes for SPH Media Trust and how will the Government track the progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what will be done to ensure the viability of our vernacular news media, given their limited local market sizes; (b) how will the Ministry (i) ensure that our vernacular news media has enough resources, talent and technology to continue to produce good quality news and (ii) create opportunities for our vernacular news media to grow beyond Singapore readership; and (c) how does vernacular news media remain relevant, given the declining use of vernacular languages amongst our younger generations.

sections.label: SPH Media Trust restructuring complete
sections.summary: The restructuring process is complete and the new SPH Media Trust shared its plans with the public about two weeks ago.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The restructuring process is complete and the new SPH Media Trust, or SMT, shared its plans with the public about two weeks ago.

sections.label: SMT reach and trust survey
sections.summary: A survey last year found SMT's weekly reach extends to almost 75% of Singaporeans, and three in four Singaporeans trust SMT for reliable news and content.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Based on a survey last year, SMT’s weekly reach extends to almost 75% of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Three in four Singaporeans trust SMT to produce reliable news and content.

sections.label: Global print advertising revenue decline
sections.summary: Globally, print advertising revenue is declining 7% year-on-year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Globally, print advertising revenue is declining 7% year-on-year.

sections.label: SMT fact-checking and literacy programmes
sections.summary: SMT will set up a fact-checking service to debunk fake news and launch media awareness and financial literacy programmes for the public.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SMT will set up a fact-checking service to debunk fake news and launch media awareness and financial literacy programmes for the public.

sections.label: Government funding for SMT newsrooms
sections.summary: Government funding for SMT will sustain vernacular newsrooms and develop new content formats like videos and podcasts to reach younger generations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Government funding for SMT will go towards sustaining vernacular newsrooms and developing new content formats like videos and podcasts, to reach the younger generations.

sections.label: MCI funding support for SMT
sections.summary: MCI has set aside up to $180 million annually over five years, with SMT expected to spend about 40% initially on tech and digital talent.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MCI has, therefore, set aside funding support of up to $180 million annually, over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In its initial years, we expect SMT to spend approximately 40% of the funding on tech investments and digital talent.

sections.label: MCI monitoring SMT performance
sections.summary: MCI will monitor SMT through KPIs on reach, engagement, vernacular and youth reach, and product resilience, with half-yearly reports and a five-year funding review.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: With such a significant amount of public funding, MCI will monitor SMT's performance closely through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) that track total reach and engagement of SMT’s products, with a focus on their digital platforms; specific reach indicators for vernacular groups and youths; and resilience of SMT’s flagship products to minimise downtime and disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: SMT is required to provide progress update reports to MCI on a half-yearly basis.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This allows MCI to track their progress and for the Government to help achieve its desired outcomes when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will also review the funding quantum after the first five years, based on the progress that SMT has made.

sections.label: Trust in CNA
sections.summary: The 2021 Reuters Institute Digital News Report indicated that 79% of respondents expressed trust in CNA.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In fact, the 2021 edition of the Reuters Institute Digital News Report indicated that 79% of respondents expressed trust in CNA.

sections.label: Ceasing Lianhe Wanbao publication
sections.summary: After a strategic review, SMT decided to cease Lianhe Wanbao and focus on Shin Min, while committing to continued print access.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Some of the moves that they have taken are practical and sensible ones, such as, assessing whether it makes sense for them to continue to have two evening papers, Shin Min Daily News and Lianhe Wanbao.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And after a careful strategic review, looking at the reach of both evening papers and satisfying their own desire to ensure that the evening papers continue to reach a wide enough audience, decided that they will cease the publication of Lianhe Wanbao by focusing on Shin Min instead.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These kinds of decisions, I think, will continue to be taken, if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But SMT as well as the Government are committed to ensuring that even those who access news mainly through print will be able to do so on a continued basis.

sections.label: Disbursement depends on SMT investments
sections.summary: Disbursement depends on SMT's specific investments and MCI's satisfaction, up to $180 million annually and up to $900 million over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: What is actually going to be disbursed will depend on the specific investments that SMT makes, through their progress updates to MCI, whether we are satisfied that these are the right things to do and that they will produce or they have the likelihood of producing good results.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, it is up to $180 million annually and, therefore, up to $900 million over five years.

sections.label: Local media trust and competition
sections.summary: A Member asks whether local media is competitive and whether consumers exercise choice by not buying local publications, necessitating public funds for SMT.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: She mentioned that she felt that there was trust in our local media.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am wondering: (a) if she would also argue that our local media marketplace is generally competitive; and, hence, part (b) of my question would be, if that is so, whether consumers are actually exercising their choice, but perhaps they do not entirely trust the local media, with not purchasing the various publications of our local media outlets, which has, therefore, necessitated this usage of public funds to fund SMT.

sections.label: Translating eyeballs into dollars
sections.summary: The passage states that worldwide, including the New York Times and The Guardian, it is very hard to translate eyeballs into dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is worldwide, whether it is in the US with the New York Times, or in the UK with The Guardian.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is very hard to translate eyeballs into dollars.

sections.label: Figures since 1998
sections.summary: The passage states that since 1998 they tried to be in the black, managed only in 2019, and last year cut 12% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And the figures I quoted, since 1998, they have been trying to be in the black.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They managed to only in 2019, after two decades of transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And even then, last year, they had to cut people, 12% of the workforce.
